posts.cooked: Sorry to disappoint, folks...I had no intention of arguing this statistics thing, because it doesn't really pertain to this issue.  A game of SOTM is not a roulette wheel...heroes' HP starts the game at a predetermined amount, so there are relatively narrow ranges of possible outcomes.  In a sufficiently large number of SOTM games, it's extremely probable that Voss will end up double-punching a hero at some point...it's built into the game's mechanics, especially with characters like the Scholar that are built for tanking, and cards like Smoke Bombs that encourage players to stay at the same HP total.  The text of the cards, not exclusively luck, will be what determines whether this situation arises...if you fight Voss more than twice or thrice, it's extremely likely you'll see this happen, or at least be able to tell that it could have.

One thing about the break-outs though, they tend to start mid-stream (of course).  This one, for example, references a scenario that we can't see because it's still back in the original thread.  If you weren't following the original topic thread, you may have a hard time figuring out what the heck is going on.

This is one of many deficiencies with this forum software, compared to Simple Machine Forums or PHPBB.  In addition to having better subscription functions, which can find all the threads you've ever posted in rather than only the ones you personally started, it also has Quote buttons which automatically include a link to the quoted post, which remains on-target even if the quoting post is later Split into a separate topic.  As it stands, while I or a mod could find the original post that this split off from, then edit my split-off post to include a link, doing so would have to be done by hand, a tedious and laborious process (which, in my case, would be further complicated by my browser's tendency to crash on this website).

EDIT:  To be clear, this is not a criticism of CajunJoel; I'm sure he's doing the best he can with the software he put together.  I'm just saying that if the forum had originally been founded on some other platform, it might well have been more stable and convenient than it has turned out to be, but I completely accept that there must have been reasons why it was done the way it was.  If this was the Wizards of the Coast website, I'd be (and was!) far more critical of the shortcomings of their software, because I expect a large company like Hasborg to have the resources to do better.  >G gets a pass on a lot of things I wouldn't put up with elsewhere, by virtue of being like five people who have consistently proven their general excellence…I don't fault them for being less than perfect, since they're already a lot closer than many people ever try to be.
